rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī situates the Hajj command in God's charge to Abraham, the House's builder, to call all people; prophets descended from Abraham later performed the pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: باني البيت إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام عن أمر الله سبحانه وتعالى بقوله إذ قام المقام : يا ايها الناس ! كتب عليكم الحج فحجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book concealed the Hajj obligation from their scripture out of envy for the Arabs; the verse's close returns to those who knowingly conceal truth, above all the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ثم أخفاها أهل الكتاب فيما أخفوه من كتابهم حسدا للعرب وختمت آية الحج بعليم رجع إلى أمر الكاتمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance requires remorse for the sin, resolve not to return, and disclosure of what had been concealed, making repentance visible through cessation.
rows.anchor: بالندم على ارتكاب الذنب { وأصلحوا } بالعزم على عدم العود { وبينوا } ما كانوا كتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although human repentance is itself enabled by God, the verse presents it as prompting God's return: He accepts and preserves repentants, and the ongoing verb suggests continued care.
rows.anchor: أي أقبل توبتهم فأحفظهم بما يشعر به مثال الفعل الدائم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali reads the fa as signaling God's swift merciful rescue from fear and regret into intimacy; worldly fear and striving can spare the sinner from the greater punishment.
rows.anchor: فمن لم يحترق بنار الخوف أحرقته نار السطوة - أفاده الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is repeatedly Tawwāb toward one who repeatedly sins and returns, and Raḥīm toward the person who does what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: أي مرة بعد مرة لمن كر على الذنب ثم راجع التوبة كرة إثر كرة { الرحيم * } لمن فعل ما يرضيني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording broadens the condemned group from concealers to all who disbelieve, whether by concealment or another form of disbelief.
rows.anchor: { إن الذين كفروا } أي بهذا الكتمان وغيره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali infers that disbelievers usually repent, whereas concealers usually persist: the text explicitly names the concealer's repentance but passes over the disbeliever's, so it singles out the former and qualifies the latter.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ففي إشعاره يسر توبة الكافرين وعسر توبة المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dying as a disbeliever reveals an evil innate disposition; such a person deserves humiliation for that nature, not merely for a newly acquired act, and people should credit God for good and blame themselves for evil.
rows.anchor: الميت كافرا مجبول جبلة شر بين سبحانه وتعالى أنه مستحق في نفس الأمر لكل خزي لذلك لا لسبب جدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the omitted causal fa and the deictic of distance as signaling the disbelievers' expulsion.
rows.anchor: فأسقط فاء السبب وعبر عنهم بأداة البعد إشارة إلى طردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's curse means His banishment and exclusion, since He is the only sovereign.
rows.anchor: { عليهم لعنة الله } أي طرد الملك الذي لا ملك سواه وإبعاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels and all people also curse them, since everyone curses the unjust and the greatest wrongdoer is the disbeliever.
rows.anchor: { والملائكة والناس أجمعين * } أي هم أهل لذلك وكل أحد يلعن الظالم وأظلم الظالمين الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about remaining forever refers to remaining in the curse.
rows.anchor: { خالدين فيها } أي اللعنة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says their punishment is not lightened because the encompassing curse gives them two punishments: one attached to their state and another to their deed.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ذكر وصف العذاب بذكر ما لزمهم من اللعنة ليجمع لهم بين العقابين

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali explains that they receive no reprieve: punishment begins at death and is not delayed by any intervening person.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من النظرة وهو التأخير المرتقب نجازه فالمعنى أنهم لا يمهلون

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says some sinful believers have delayed punishment; worldly persistence or increase in sin corresponds to persistent or increased punishment, because the world is the field of the afterlife and recompense follows one's pattern.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ففيه إشعار بطائفة أي من عصاة المؤمنين يؤخر عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding argument, laws, and account of reward and punishment, the verse restates that God alone is the deity, without a partner able to oppose His will; this warns unbelievers and encourages the faithful.
rows.anchor: فإلهكم إله واحد لا شريك له يدافعه عما يريد لا إله غلا هو المنتقم من أعدائه العظيم في كبريائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated noun ilāh makes clear that true deity is indivisible by kind, person, attribute, action, or any other distinction.
rows.anchor: { إله واحد } أي لا ينقسم بوجه من الوجوه لا بمجانسة ولا بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula establishes oneness by negating every other deity and affirming God; no other can possibly qualify for divinity or deserve worship.
rows.anchor: فهذا تقرير للوحدانية بنفي غيره وإثباته فلا يصح بوجه ولا يمكن في عقل أن يصلح للإلهية غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmān denotes broad mercy through transient blessings given to allies and enemies alike; Raḥīm denotes special mercy through lasting blessings for God's allies.
rows.anchor: { الرحمن } أي العام الرحمة بالنعم الزائلة لأوليائه وأعدائه { الرحيم * } أي المخصص بالنعم الباقية لأوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's exclusive divinity entails possession of all greatness, majesty, and power, while His mercy makes Him the giver of every great and subtle blessing.
rows.anchor: فثبت بالتفرد بالألوهية أنه حائز بجميع العظمة وبيده مجامع الكبرياء والقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything besides God is either a blessing or a recipient of one; He alone is feared for His might and hoped in for mercy, and no one can challenge His judgments.
rows.anchor: فكل ما سواه إما نعمة أو منعم عليه , فهو المخشي سطوته المرجو رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī suggests that the waw may connect this verse to the early statement that God knows everything, before the creation of Adam, since monotheism is the chief aim and source of worship.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد عندي وإن بعد المدى أن تكون الواو في قوله { وإلهكم } عاطفة على قوله في أوائل السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads this verse as a clearer, renewed proof of oneness after the earlier argument from 2:28 onward and the intervening discussion of concealment, repentance, and recompense.
rows.anchor: فأعاد الدليل على وجه أبين من الأول وأبسط , فلما تقرر على وجه لا مطعن فيه أمر الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed proof shows that God is unlike worldly kings: He has no equal or near equal, and no subordinate can prevent His rewarding the obedient or punishing the disobedient.
rows.anchor: ليس كملوك الدنيا الذين قد يحول بينهم وبين إثابة بعض الطائعين وعقوبة بعض العاصين بعض أتباعهم , فإنه واحد لا كفؤ له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī defends this coordination as normal eloquence: a speaker may give a sufficient proof, explain its results and branches, then restate it differently if the opponent remains unconvinced; al-Bāqillānī exemplifies the method.
rows.anchor: ولا يستنكر تجويز هذا العطف لأنه جرت عادة البلغاء أن أحدهم إذا أراد إقامة الحج على شيء لأمر يرتبه عليه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali describes the book as calling people to truth and teaching God's claim over creation, while displaying the merits of God's chosen angels, prophets, messengers, and their allies as proof for their followers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ولما كان مضمون الكتاب دعوة الخلق إلى الحق , والتعريف بحق الحق على الخلق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali argues that dispersal harms people and unity benefits them; the unity of Adam, Abraham, and Muhammad gathering descendants, Islam, and religion respectively points toward the greater benefit of God's unity.
rows.anchor: وكان الضار للخلق إنما هو الشتات كان النافع لهم إنما هو الوحدة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali links visible unities, including spirit, soul, and intellect, to understanding the deeper unity of divinity, which is the foundation of every unity beneath it.
rows.anchor: وفي إفهام ذلك وحدات ما يظن في ظاهر الوحدات الظاهرة من وحدة الروح ووحدة النفس والعقل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali argues that if discord is blameworthy under one human father, it is still more blameworthy under the religious father, perfected Prophet, and the one merciful God who gathers His chosen people.
rows.anchor: فإذا قبح الشتات مع وحدة الأب الوالد فكيف به مع وحدة الأب المدين ! فكيف به مع وحدة النبي المكمل !

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says divine names ultimately converge on God's unity, to whom worshippers turn in all outward and inward needs and states; no unity is more perfect than the unseen one beyond sense and intellect, without quantity or quality.
rows.anchor: فجميع أسمائه لها وحدة تنتهي وحدتها إلى وحدة الإله الذي انتهى إليه الإله

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says experience finds rest in joining one company and fatigue in following many, whose followers' aims conflict; the greatest call to gather people is monotheism in continuity with lordship.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : وقد صح بالتجربة أن الراحة في حصبة الواحد وأن التعب في اتباع العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fighting command aims to end harm that turns Muslims from their faith, expels them, takes their property, or denies their rights; it applies to any aggressor, unbeliever or rebel, until they return to God's order.
rows.anchor: { حتى لا تكون فتنة } أي توجد فتنة بأن لا يقدروا أن يؤذوا أحدا من أهل الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here religion means obedience and worship. Because the passage came early after the Hijra, before Muslims had seen enough victory to strengthen their resolve, the statement is left without added emphasis.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا في أوائل ما بعد الهجرة قبل أن يروا من نصر الله لهم ما يقوي عزائمهم أعراه من التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For religion to belong to God means Islam is publicly dominant, Satan has no share in it, and neither unbelievers nor rebels can openly harm Muslims; polytheists are eliminated while scripturalists remain under jizya.
rows.anchor: بأن يكون أمر المسلمين ظاهرا , ليس للشيطان فيه نصيب , لا يقدر أحد من أهل الكفر ولا أهل البغي على التظاهر بأذى أحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripturalists may remain because, despite distortion, their books retain guidance for those whom God enables to see truth; idolaters have no such guide, so leaving them would only increase certain shirk without benefit.
rows.anchor: قد بقي فيها ما يهدي الموفق لأنها لم يعمها التحريف , وأما أهل الأوثان فليس لهم ما يرشدهم إلى الحق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali sees the true party continuing to fight the rebellious party throughout the Muhammadan era to remove discord and establish God's religion in monotheism, contentment, and the way of the righteous predecessors and prophetic caliphate.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ففي طيه إشعار بما وقع وهو واقع وسيقع من قتال طائفة الحق لطائفة البغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents desist, they have abandoned the injustice that warranted fighting; then there is no ground to fight them.
rows.anchor: { فإن انتهوا } أي كلفوا أنفسهم الرجوع عما استوجبوا به القتال فقد تركوا الظلم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali explains nahy as a restraining judgment that prevents a person from the act toward which the self inclines, and cites the Prophet's instruction to give precedence to people of understanding and discernment.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي الحكم المانع من الفعل المترامي إليه بمنزلة أثر العقل المسمى نهى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says injustice broadly means placing anything out of its proper position, from the highest matters of religion to the lowest.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فذكر الظلم الشامل لوجوه إيقاع الأمر في غير موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī allows an alternate implication: if they cease associating partners with God, do not attack them; if Muslims attack them, they become the wrongdoers subject to retaliation themselves.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير : فإن انتهوا عن الشرك فقد انتفى عنهم اسم الظلم فلا تعتدوا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ʿudwān means fighting with utmost force, speed, and determination.
rows.anchor: ومعنى العدوان القتال بغاية العدو والشدة والعزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred month repaid by a sacred month refers to fighting in Dhu al-Qaʿdah of year seven if the opponents fought in Dhu al-Qaʿdah of year six and blocked the Ḥudaybiyya pilgrimage; this frames the ʿUmrat al-Qaḍāʾ.
rows.anchor: وهو ذو القعدة من سنة سبع إن قاتلتموهم فيه لكونهم قاتلوكم في شهر حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanctities are all matters to be protected and respected; retaliation requires matching the violation in kind and measure.
rows.anchor: { والحرمات } أي كلها وهي جمع حرمة وهي ما يحفظ ويرعى ولا ينتهك { قصاص } أي تتبع للمساواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who deliberately harms Muslims may be answered in proportion to the harm at any time or place; calling the response aggression is rhetorical matching that strengthens resolve.
rows.anchor: { فمن } أي فتسبب عن هذا أنه من { اعتدى عليكم } أي تعمد أذاكم في شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'against you' blocks the objection that one may repay an attack on someone else with the worst harm suffered by anyone; retaliation is limited to what was done to the person addressed.
rows.anchor: ولعله أعاد الظرف وإن أفهمه الأول لدفع تعنت من لعله يقول : الكلام شامل لاعتدائه علي وعلى غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because equality in retaliation is hard to maintain once anger rises, God commands careful restraint and reminds them that He is with the pious, whether they keep the limit or forgive.
rows.anchor: ولما جعل المماثلة حدا وكان أمرها خفيا والوقوف عنده بعد استرسال النفس بإرسالها صعبا حذر من تعديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī invokes the maxim that forgiving a wrongdoer adds honor, reinforcing the call to pardon.
rows.anchor: وما زاد الله عبدا بعفو إلا عزا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali sees the verse as opening a path to the virtue of forgiveness, including maintaining ties with one who severs them and pardoning the wrongdoer; God replaces the self's desires for those who persist in piety.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ففي ضمنه إشعار وتطريق لمقصد السماح الذي هو خير الفضائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending is one of jihad's main supports, but early Muslims had little money and feared that spending would ruin them, as Satan suggested; God corrects that assumption.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت النفقة من أعظم دعائم الجهاد وكان العيش في أول الإسلام ضيقا والمال قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī links the pilgrimage command to the Kaaba as a return-place, Safa and Marwa, and the appointed times for pilgrimage; the surrounding fighting verses lead toward those rites and recall the Ḥudaybiyya obstruction.
rows.anchor: و { مواقيت للناس والحج } ولا سيما وآيات القتال هذه إنما نظمت ههنا بسببهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence implies: perform Hajj and ʿUmrah even if obstructed, and fight those who fight you on the pilgrimage route so the way opens; after the conquest made completion possible, the verse says to complete them.
rows.anchor: فحجوا واعتمروا أي تلبسوا بذلك وإن صددتم عنه وقاتلوا في سبيل الله من قاتلكم في وجهكم ذلك لينفتح لكم السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing Hajj and ʿUmrah means carrying out their rites, limits, conditions, and recommended practices.
rows.anchor: { الحج والعمرة } بمناسكهما وحدودهما وشرائطهما وسننهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'for God' makes clear that the preceding spending and fighting serve worship for God alone; Biquāʿī avoids a pronoun so the dedication is not restricted by a qualifier.
rows.anchor: { لله } الملك الذي لا كفوء له أي لذاته , ولم يضمر لئلا يتقيد بقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive conditional 'if you are prevented' covers any interruption, since the legal ruling depends on the occurrence rather than a named agent; the conditional form signals that this is uncommon.
rows.anchor: { فإن أحصرتم } أي منعتم وحبستم عن إتمامها , من الإحصار وهو منع العدو المحصر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali explains iḥṣār as being prevented or confined from completing the rites, like illness confining someone from acting in their affairs.
rows.anchor: من الإحصار وهو منع العدو المحصر عن متصرفه كالمرض يحصره عن التصرف في شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pilgrim prevented from completing the rites who wishes to leave iḥrām owes an easily available sacrificial animal from camel, cattle, or sheep, slaughtered where blocked and given in charity.
rows.anchor: فالواجب على المحصر الذي منع عن إكماله تلافيا لما وقع له من الخلل في عملهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaysara means that the required animal is found with ease, as though it sought its own ease; yusr is what comes without burden.
rows.anchor: أي وجد يسرة على غاية السهولة حتى كأنه طالب يسر نفسه , واليسر حصول الشيء عفوا بلا كلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to shave applies to the hair of anyone in iḥrām for Hajj or ʿUmrah.
rows.anchor: أي شعرها إذا كنتم محرمين بحج أو عمرة , من الحلق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali defines shaving as removing what can be removed by cutting with an effective tool, and says the head is the gathered structure of the body or of any thing.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو إزالة ما يتأتى للزوال بالقطع من الآلة الماضية في عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrifice reaches its place of slaughter: wherever a pilgrim is blocked if in iḥṣār, otherwise at Marwa, Mina, or a similar place.
rows.anchor: أي الموضع الذي يحل ذبحه فيه , إن كنتم محصرين فحيث أحصرتم وإلا فعند المروة أو في منى ونحوهما

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali defines hady as an offering by which the lower approaches the higher, an animal ransom presented to God and directed to the Ancient House.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والهدي ما تقرب به الأدنى للأعلى وهو اسم ما يتخذ فداء من الأنعام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked whether to shave or slaughter first, the Prophet answered, 'Do it; there is no harm,' because both acts share the broad meaning of ransom.
rows.anchor: قال : ( افعل ولا حرج ) , لأن الجميع غاية بالمعنى الشامل للفداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the religion easy through the Prophet's blessing, so someone ill or suffering harm on the head may take the needed relief.
rows.anchor: وكان الله سبحانه وتعالى قد وضع عنا الآصار ببركة النبي المختار صلى الله عليه وسلم فجعل دينه يسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concession applies to illness for which shaving is beneficial or to even slight discomfort on the head, such as lice or another cause.
rows.anchor: { مريضا } يرجى له بالحلق خير { أو به أذى } ولو قل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fidya is the compensatory act owed for shaving or treating the condition with something forbidden in iḥrām.
rows.anchor: { ففدية } أي فعلية بحلق رأسه أو المداواة بما نهى المحرم عنه فدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pilgrim may choose three days of fasting, feeding six needy people three sāʿs of food, or sacrificing livestock; charity is the equivalent of fasting when fasting is unavailable.
rows.anchor: { من صيام } لثلاثة أيام { أو صدقة } لثلاثة آصع من طعام على ستة مساكين

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali explains the food measure as one sāʿ per day: two meals, each two mudd, so three days provide three sāʿs.
rows.anchor: ولليوم وجبتا فطر وسحور , لكل وجبة مدان فلكل يوم صاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusuk means drawing near to God by slaughtering an animal; the three forms of fidya are alternatives.
rows.anchor: أي تقرب بذبح شيء من الأنعام وهذه فدية مخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from 'if prevented' to 'when secure' marks security as expected and certain: the obstacle and illness have passed, and the active form urges gratitude.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى ذلك بأداة التحقيق بعد تعبيره عن الإحصار بأداة الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattuʿ is enjoying lawful status after performing ʿUmrah during the Hajj months while traveling at least a shortening distance; the pilgrim remains lawful after reaching the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: { فمن تمتع } أي تلذذ باستباحة دخوله إلى الحرم بإحرامه في أشهر الحج على مسافة القصر من الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pilgrim then enters Hajj from Mecca during that same year without returning to the appointed miqat.
rows.anchor: أي إحرامه به من عامة ذلك من مكة المشرفة من غير رجوع إلى الميقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tamattuʿ sacrifice compensates for enjoying a period of release between the two rites while traveling; a qārin combines both rites in one journey, though they normally occur at separate times of release and iḥrām.
rows.anchor: هذا لمتمتع وأما القارن فلجمعه بين النسكين في سفر واحد وشأنهما أن يكونا في وقتين وقت حل ووقت حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording supports appending Hajj to ʿUmrah, moving from the lesser state of consecration to the greater one.
rows.anchor: وفي العبارة إشعار بصحة إرداف الحج على العمرة لأنه ترق من إحرام أدنى إلى إحرام أعلى
